summary: Office Wi‑Fi client aggregation interacts with NAT timeouts causing ephemeral port reuse and SSH connection resets to internal hosts
description: Several engineers in the SF office reported intermittent SSH resets and failures when connecting to internal build hosts (10.3.4.0/22) while connected to the corporate Wi‑Fi. Connections over wired ethernet to the same hosts are stable. Initial hypothesis: wireless aggregation/A-MPDU interaction with the branch NAT and our UDP hole-punching for VPN is leading to ephemeral port reuse and mid-session TCP/SSH resets.
impact: Multiple engineering users in office unable to maintain stable SSH sessions to internal build/test infrastructure. CI jobs running from laptops occasionally drop during deploys. Affects productivity; no public customer impact detected.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Connect a laptop to corp‑wifi (SF office, 802.11ax APs). 2) Establish site-to-site VPN via corporate edge (WireGuard client from laptop). 3) SSH to an internal build host behind branch NAT (10.3.4.x). 4) Start an interactive session and run a long-running command (e.g., tail -f + large scp). 5) Observe intermittent SSH disconnects after ~300-1200s. Repeat with wired ethernet — issue does not reproduce.
observed_behavior: SSH sessions drop with 'Connection reset by peer' or 'Broken pipe'. netstat on branch edge shows ephemeral port mappings being reclaimed and reused rapidly. AP telemetry shows high A-MPDU aggregation sizes and bursty TX patterns for affected clients. NAT table entries time out unusually quickly for UDP/VPN flows on the branch gateway during the bursts.
expected_behavior: SSH sessions should remain stable over Wi‑Fi; NAT should preserve ephemeral mappings for the negotiated lifetime; wireless aggregation should not trigger premature NAT eviction.
logs:
branch-gateway/syslog: Mar 10 10:42:11 natd[1223]: evicting entry UDP 10.3.4.23:51734 -> 34.67.12.9:51820 (age 8s)
ap-telemetry: client 02:11:22:33:44:55 a-mpdu: avg 64k, bursts: 12 in 60s
laptop dmesg: wireguard: peer 34.67.12.9 handshake OK; keepalive every 25s
ssh client: Mar 10 10:49:21 packet_write_wait: Connection to 10.3.4.45 port 22: Broken pipe
investigation_notes:
- Reproduced with two different laptop models and two different APs in SF office.
- Packet captures show that when AP sends large aggregated frames, bursts of ACK-less UDP keepalives are delayed (driver coalescing), causing branch gateway to see no activity for VPN UDP mapping and prune it.
- NAT eviction policy on branch gateway uses inactivity thresholds of 10s for UDP by default; aggressive pruning combined with delayed keepalives leads to a race where ephemeral ports are reclaimed and later reassigned to new flows. When reassigned, inbound packets land on the wrong TCP tuple causing upstream TCP resets.
- Wired path shows no aggregation; keepalives are timely and NAT entries persist.
- Configuring laptop wireguard keepalive to 10s reduced occurrence but did not eliminate it under heavy aggregation bursts.
- No related recent code deploys in networking infra; change window: AP firmware update two weeks ago that enabled higher TX aggregation sizes on 802.11ax under heavy client load.
- Correlated increase in incidents with AP firmware rollouts (ticket AP-FW-2026-02-25).
actions_taken:
1) Temporarily adjusted branch NAT UDP inactivity timeout from 10s -> 60s for SF office gateway (mitigated immediate flapping).
2) Contacted wireless team to throttle A-MPDU max aggregation per-client to default levels on affected APs (rolled back recent aggressive setting).
3) Recommended laptop-side workarounds: set WireGuard PersistentKeepalive to 15s and reduce driver TX coalescing (sysctl/net driver knobs) where feasible.
4) Scheduled follow-up: firmware vendor validation of aggregation vs keepalive interplay and vendor bug report ID: VENDOR-1823.
comments: Maya Chen | 2026-03-10: Reported initial symptom — SSH resets while on corp‑wifi. Attached packet capture and screen recording of ssh disconnects.
Luca Romano | 2026-03-11: Started reproducibility testing. Reproduced on AP‑B1 and AP‑B2. Captured pcap on branch edge and AP. Noticed NAT evictions correlated with large A‑MPDU bursts.
SRE Oncall (Jonah Patel) | 2026-03-11: Increased NAT UDP timeout to 60s on sf-branch-gw as a short-term mitigation. Observed immediate drop in user reports.
Wireless Team (Aisha Raman) | 2026-03-12: Rolled back AP aggregation parameter 'tx_aggregation_max' from 256->64 on the affected radios. Monitoring for regressions.
Maya Chen | 2026-03-13: Confirmed SSH sessions stable for daily workflows after NAT timeout increase + AP rollback. Still collecting telemetry for full closure.
resolution: Mitigation applied: NAT UDP inactivity timeout increased and AP aggregation parameter rolled back. Short-term workaround documented for engineers (set persistent keepalive). Long-term fixes: vendor patch expected to address interaction; plan to add a NAT heuristic to avoid reclaiming recently used UDP mappings for flows identified as VPN tunnels.
postmortem_followup:
- Track vendor bug VENDOR-1823 and schedule patch validation.
- Implement NAT heuristics in branch gateway to detect and protect VPN UDP mappings.
- Add monitoring alert for increased NAT eviction rates and correlate with AP aggregation telemetry.
- Update runbook: recommend WireGuard keepalives and client-side driver knobs for on-prem office Wi‑Fi.
